newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends steady-up amid commercial buying.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends steady-up amid commercial buying.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled unchanged to higher, with nearby March buoyed by commercial buying, traders said.

"Strength in our March came on commercial pricing by Cargill and Continental. It's interesting to note that CIS was the featured buyer yesterday as well -- so the question is, what business do they see around the corner?" a trader said.

Traders said March had been under pressure from cash basis levels in Kansas City, which were two cents per bushel lower except on high-protein wheat. Deferred contracts also saw spillover pressure from CBOT soybeans.
KCBT wheat settled steady to three cents per bushel higher, with March up three cents at $4.15-3/4. May gained 1/2 cent to close at $3.76-1/2. July was unchanged at $3.56.
Traders said Cargill, Inc bought 1.3 million KCBT March bushels Wednesday. Wolcott Lincoln bought 1.5 million July. Continental bull-spread 700,000 March/July at 59 cents.
Traders said the March/July spread tested but failed to close above psychological resistance at 60 cents per bushel. It closed at 56-3/4 cents.
